rule: Long run <= 30% of weekly miles (from 20 mi/week up).
summary: No study found tests the long run as a share of weekly mileage. The best evidence (Frandsen 2025) puts the injury signal in a single run's length relative to the longest recent run, which the spike cap already enforces; the 30% share only shapes how the week is distributed. Cheap and conventional, so keep as a labelled heuristic; revisit if it blocks the long-run length the marathon block needs.

sources.note: Risk tied to single-run length vs 30-day longest, not to its share of the week
No consistent link between distance/duration parameters and injury; caution on prescribing specific parameters
